B2-1-0.name: Feed the verb
B2-1-0.prompt: Completa cada verbo con un gerundio sobre tu propia familia y luego di la misma idea después de una preposición.
answers: I can’t stand being interrupted at dinner. / I’m tired of being interrupted at dinner.
My brother keeps borrowing my clothes. / He never apologises for borrowing my clothes.
We’ve given up arguing about politics. / We’re tired of arguing about politics.
I’m good at calming everyone down. / My family relies on me for calming everyone down.
Nobody here objects to sharing the cooking. / Everybody is happy about sharing the cooking.

B2-1-1.name: Frame it first
B2-1-1.prompt: Di cada idea dos veces: primero como una frase simple y luego reformulada con una cláusula nominal después de “be”.
items: they still argue about the house
answers: Nobody apologised. / The problem is that nobody apologised.
My sister moved abroad. / The truth is that my sister moved abroad.
We only meet at weddings. / The sad thing is that we only meet at weddings.
He forgot my birthday. / What hurt me was that he forgot my birthday.
They still argue about the house. / The issue is that they still argue about the house.

B2-2-0.name: Did it happen?
B2-2-0.prompt: Para cada indicación, di la frase y luego explica si la acción se realizó o no.
items: hand in the form / obligatory, done
bring a gift / brought one unnecessarily
tell the manager / not done, regretted
answers: We had to hand in the form. (It was obligatory, and we did.)
We didn’t have to pay the deposit. (It wasn’t required, so we didn’t pay it.)
I needn’t have brought a gift. (I brought one, but it wasn’t necessary.)
I should have told the manager. (I didn’t, and I regret it.)
She was supposed to lock the door. (She was expected to, but she forgot.)

B2-2-1.name: Three levels of certainty
B2-2-1.prompt: Para cada pista, da tres explicaciones: una casi segura, una posible y una que puedes descartar.
items: his coat is still on the chair
all the lights are on at midnight
her phone goes straight to voicemail
the window is open from the inside
answers: He must have left in a hurry. / He might have gone to a meeting. / He can’t have gone home without his coat.
Someone must have been hungry. / The kids might have eaten it. / It can’t have been the dog — it can’t reach the table.
Someone must have forgotten to turn them off. / They might have had a party. / They can’t have been asleep.
Her battery must have died. / She might have switched it off. / She can’t have blocked me — we spoke an hour ago.
Someone inside must have opened it. / It might have been the cleaner. / It can’t have been a burglar from outside.

B2-3-0.name: Commas or no commas
B2-3-0.prompt: Une cada par en una sola frase y di si la cláusula necesita comas y por qué.
items: I visited Porto. It sits on a river.
The street was too steep. We stayed on it.
My cousin lives in Cali. He never leaves.
That’s the museum. It opened last year.
This is the year. Everything changed then.
answers: I visited Porto, which sits on a river. (Commas: Porto is already identified; this is extra information.)
The street (that) we stayed on was too steep. (No commas: the clause tells us which street.)
My cousin, who lives in Cali, never leaves. (Commas if I have one cousin; the clause is extra information.)
That’s the museum that opened last year. (No commas: the clause identifies which museum.)
This is the year when everything changed. (No commas: the clause identifies which year.)

B2-3-1.name: Stack three, stack four
B2-3-1.prompt: Describe cada cosa con tres adjetivos en el orden correcto y luego agrega un cuarto sin romper el orden.
answers: a tall old brick building → a tall old red brick building
a small bright square room → a small bright square white room
a colourful little wooden stall → a colourful little old wooden stall
a beautiful long stone bridge → a beautiful long old stone bridge
a cosy small traditional café → a cosy small old traditional Colombian café

B2-3-2.name: Same contrast, three ways
B2-3-2.prompt: Expresa cada contraste tres veces: con despite, con although y con however.
items: far from the centre / well connected
answers: Despite the price, it’s worth it. / Although it’s expensive, it’s worth it. / It’s expensive. However, it’s worth it.
Despite the noise, it’s lively. / Although it’s noisy, it’s lively. / It’s noisy. However, it’s lively.
Despite being far from the centre, it’s well connected. / Although it’s far from the centre, it’s well connected. / It’s far from the centre. However, it’s well connected.
Despite its size, it’s never boring. / Although it’s small, it’s never boring. / It’s small. However, it’s never boring.
Despite the rain, it’s beautiful. / Although it’s rainy, it’s beautiful. / It’s rainy. However, it’s beautiful.

B2-4-0.name: Cut the subject
B2-4-0.prompt: Reduce cada cláusula si los sujetos coinciden; si no coinciden, escribe “can’t reduce” y explica por qué.
items: While I was waiting, I answered emails.
After she left, the meeting improved.
Before I go to bed, I read.
When the alarm went off, I ignored it.
Since I moved here, I sleep better.
answers: While waiting, I answered emails.
Can’t reduce: the subjects are different (she / the meeting).
Before going to bed, I read.
Can’t reduce: the subjects are different (the alarm / I).
Since moving here, I sleep better.

B2-4-1.name: Reason, then condition
B2-4-1.prompt: Dale a cada hecho una cláusula de razón y luego reformúlalo como una condición.
items: I go to bed at ten
answers: Since I get up at six, I go to bed at ten. / If I want to feel rested, I go to bed at ten.
I skip breakfast because I’m never hungry in the morning. / Unless I’m really hungry, I skip breakfast.
As I sleep well at night, I never nap. / As long as I sleep seven hours, I never nap.
Because it’s quiet, I work best at night. / Provided that nobody calls, I work best at night.
I hate Monday mornings because I have three meetings. / If I have meetings early, I hate Monday mornings.

B2-5-0.name: Judge the behaviour
B2-5-0.prompt: Comenta cada comportamiento dos veces: una de forma general y otra nombrando a la persona con of o for.
answers: It’s rude to interrupt a colleague. / It was rude of him to interrupt his colleague.
It’s brave to admit a mistake. / It was brave of her to admit her mistake.
It’s annoying to receive unwanted advice. / It was unkind of him to give her unwanted advice.
It’s a mistake to say nothing in a meeting. / It’s hard for new staff to say anything in a meeting.
It’s useful to ask a direct question. / It’s difficult for me to ask a direct question.

B2-5-1.name: Activity as subject
B2-5-1.prompt: Convierte cada comportamiento en un sujeto con gerundio y termina la frase con un juicio.
answers: Interrupting in meetings is disrespectful.
Replying within a minute makes you look always available.
Asking personal questions can make people uncomfortable.
Saying nothing when you’re annoyed only makes things worse.
Apologising twice sounds insincere.

B2-6-0.name: Dated or not
B2-6-0.prompt: Di cada hecho dos veces: una con un momento pasado definido y otra dentro de un tiempo no terminado, cambiando el tiempo verbal.
answers: The newspaper published a correction yesterday. / The newspaper has published two corrections this week.
We interviewed the witness last Monday. / We’ve interviewed three witnesses so far.
The reporter lost a key source in 2023. / The reporter has lost two sources this year.
She won an award last year. / She has won three awards in her career.
The paper printed a retraction this morning at eight. / The paper has printed a retraction today.

B2-6-1.name: How many or how long
B2-6-1.prompt: Para cada elemento, haz una frase con un número y otra con una duración, eligiendo la forma correcta en cada caso.
answers: She has written four articles this month. / She has been writing articles since January.
We have interviewed six witnesses. / We have been interviewing witnesses for two weeks.
I have read about fifty documents. / I have been reading documents all morning.
He has covered three days of the trial. / He has been covering the trial since Monday.
We have sent two emails to the ministry. / We have been waiting for a reply for ten days.

B2-6-2.name: Which came first
B2-6-2.prompt: Une cada par de eventos pasados en una sola frase y marca el más antiguo con el pasado perfecto.
items: the lawyers wrote / the editor apologised
we found the file / they denied it existed
he deleted the account / the reporters noticed
answers: When we published, the source had already called.
When the story appeared, she had already resigned.
The editor apologised after the lawyers had written to him.
They denied the file existed, but we had already found it.
When the reporters noticed, he had already deleted the account.

B2-7-0.name: Tag it
B2-7-0.prompt: Agrega la coletilla correcta a cada frase y dila dos veces: una para confirmar información y otra para invitar a estar de acuerdo.
items: There aren’t any settings for that
answers: Everyone has a smartphone, don’t they?
You didn’t accept the cookies, did you?
There aren’t any settings for that, are there?
She’s been offline all week, hasn’t she?
Let’s check the permissions, shall we?

B2-7-1.name: Soften the opinion
B2-7-1.prompt: Convierte cada opinión directa en una pregunta negativa y luego di si estás invitando a estar de acuerdo o expresando sorpresa.
answers: Don’t you think children get phones too early? (inviting agreement)
Isn’t it amazing that nobody reads privacy policies? (expressing surprise)
Don’t you think the regulation is useless? (inviting agreement)
Aren’t we all addicted, really? (inviting agreement)
Isn’t it scary how much the companies know? (expressing surprise)

B2-7-2.name: Hide the agent, then bring it back
B2-7-2.prompt: Di cada hecho dos veces: una en pasiva sin agente y otra con el agente de vuelta para darle énfasis.
answers: The data is being collected. / The app is collecting the data, not the government.
The accounts have been closed. / The bank has closed the accounts, not the users.
The software is being tested. / Independent engineers are testing the software.
The report will be published next month. / The minister herself will publish the report.
The policy has been changed. / The new CEO has changed the policy.

B2-8-0.name: Cut it down
B2-8-0.prompt: Reduce cada cláusula relativa o explica por qué no se puede reducir.
items: the participants who were waiting in the corridor
the method that was used in the study
the theory which explains the effect
anyone who wants to take part
answers: the participants waiting in the corridor
the method used in the study
Can’t reduce to -ing: “who” is the object. You can only drop the pronoun: the professor I interviewed.
the theory explaining the effect
anyone wanting to take part

B2-8-1.name: Add the comment
B2-8-1.prompt: Termina cada frase con “, which…” comentando toda la idea, no solo el último sustantivo.
items: The experiment was repeated three times
She remembered every name in the room
The data was lost in a software update
The results were published without review
answers: The experiment was repeated three times, which made the results more reliable.
She remembered every name in the room, which impressed everyone.
The data was lost in a software update, which meant starting from scratch.
Nobody asked the obvious question, which was surprising.
The results were published without review, which worried many scientists.

B2-9-0.name: Two cultures, one sentence
B2-9-0.prompt: Contrasta los dos hábitos en una sola frase, usando un conector diferente cada vez.
items: lunch at one / lunch at three
dinner guests arrive early / arrive late
answers: Here people have lunch at one, whereas in Spain they have it at three.
Unlike my parents, who prefer phone calls, I send voice notes.
While people are formal at work, they’re very informal afterwards.
In some countries dinner guests arrive early, whereas here they always arrive late.
Tipping is expected in the US. Here it’s unusual, except in restaurants.

B2-9-1.name: State or action
B2-9-1.prompt: Para cada elemento, di si es un estado o una acción repetida y usa la forma correcta, o las dos si ambas son posibles.
items: spend every August at the coast
answers: State: We used to live in a smaller town. (would is not possible)
Repeated action: I used to walk to school. / I would walk to school.
State: I used to be afraid of the dark. (would is not possible)
Repeated action: We used to spend every August at the coast. / We would spend every August at the coast.
State: We used to have a landline. (would is not possible)

B2-10-0.name: Front the complaint
B2-10-0.prompt: Convierte cada queja en una cláusula con what y luego otra vez con “the thing that…”.
answers: What annoys me is that the delivery never arrived. / The thing that annoys me is that the delivery never arrived.
What bothers me is that nobody answers emails. / The thing that bothers me is that nobody answers emails.
What made me angry was that the price changed at checkout. / The thing that made me angry was that the price changed at checkout.
What frustrated me was that the repair took three weeks. / The thing that frustrated me was that the repair took three weeks.
What upset me was that the apology was automated. / The thing that upset me was that the apology was automated.

B2-10-1.name: Make it indirect
B2-10-1.prompt: Convierte cada pregunta directa en una indirecta, usando una introducción diferente cada vez.
answers: Could you tell me where the manager is?
I’d like to know why I was charged twice.
Do you know when it will arrive?
Would you mind telling me who signed this off?
I was wondering whether there is a refund policy.

B2-11-0.name: Would you, though
B2-11-0.prompt: Responde cada dilema con un condicional completo y luego agrega una condición que cambiaría tu respuesta.
items: you find a wallet in the street
a friend asks you to lie for them
you’re offered a job you’re unqualified for
answers: If I found a wallet in the street, I’d take it to the police. / But if there were no ID inside, I might keep it.
If a friend asked me to lie for them, I wouldn’t do it. / I’d only do it if they were in real danger.
If I saw a colleague stealing, I’d talk to them first. / If it happened again, I’d tell the manager.
If I were offered a job I wasn’t qualified for, I’d be honest about it. / But if they offered training, I’d accept.
If I were given money by mistake, I’d return it. / Even if it were a small amount, I’d give it back.

B2-11-1.name: Present or past regret
B2-11-1.prompt: Para cada elemento, haz un deseo sobre el presente y otro sobre el pasado.
answers: I wish I spoke better English. / I wish I had studied English at school.
I wish I could talk to my brother about it. / I wish I hadn’t avoided that conversation.
I wish I lived closer to the sea. / I wish I had moved to Santa Marta years ago.
I wish I had a more interesting job. / I wish I hadn’t turned down that job in Bogotá.
I wish my sister would forgive me. / I wish I hadn’t said those things in anger.

B2-12-0.name: By then
B2-12-0.prompt: Haz una frase en futuro perfecto con una fecha límite para cada elemento y luego otra en futuro perfecto continuo con una duración.
answers: By June I’ll have finished this course. / By June I’ll have been studying English for two years.
By next year I’ll have lived in this city for a decade. / By next year I’ll have been living here for ten years.
By the end of the year I’ll have learned to drive. / By then I’ll have been taking lessons for six months.
By 2028 I’ll have paid off my student loan. / By then I’ll have been paying it for five years.
By next April I’ll have worked here for eight years. / By next April I’ll have been working in the same job for eight years.

B2-12-1.name: Two time frames
B2-12-1.prompt: Construye una frase para cada elemento con una condición pasada y un resultado presente, y luego invierte los tiempos.
items: a city you didn’t move to
a person you lost touch with
answers: If I had taken the photography course, I’d be working as a photographer now. / If I were more creative, I would have taken the course.
If I had moved to Medellín, I’d have a better job now. / If I weren’t so attached to Bogotá, I would have moved.
If I hadn’t stopped studying French, I’d be fluent now. / If I were more disciplined, I wouldn’t have stopped.
If I had accepted the offer, I’d be living in Canada now. / If I didn’t love my family so much, I would have accepted it.
If I hadn’t lost touch with Camila, she’d still be my best friend. / If I were better at keeping in touch, I wouldn’t have lost her.
